title: Energy Budgeting
hook: Doing strategy at 4pm and email at 9am is backwards for most of us.
statement: Schedule tasks by your energy, not just by open time slots.
explainer: An hour isn't just an hour. The same task is easier and better when your energy is high. Spending peak hours on admin is a quiet tax on your best work.
sop: Track your energy every hour for 3 to 5 days.
Sort tasks into high-focus and low-focus buckets.
Put high-focus work in your top 2 energy hours.
Block those hours on your calendar by task type.
Score Energy and Efficiency weekly and adjust the map.
equation_example: Energy 8, Efficiency 6. 8 × 6 = 48. Higher means you're doing your best work while you're actually sharp. Lower means you're burnt out or coasting through hours that could do more.
question: Write down your two best energy hours and what you'll protect them for.
closing_statement: Match the task to the energy, not the clock.
caption:
Principle Nº 208: Energy Budgeting

Doing strategy at 4pm and email at 9am is backwards for most of us.

Schedule tasks by your energy, not just by open time slots.
